content: The human body represents the complete physical structure of a human organism. It is composed of a head, neck, torso, two arms, and two legs, with an average height ranging from 5 to 6 feet (approximately 1.5 to 1.8 meters). This height is primarily determined by genetic factors. However, body type and body composition are influenced by postnatal factors such as diet and physical activity. The human body is commonly referred to simply as a body, while the body of a deceased individual is termed a corpse or cadaver. The human body is organized into systems, organs, tissues, and cells. The study of the structural organization and systems of the human body is known as human anatomy, whereas the study of its functional processes is referred to as physiology. Ecology, on the other hand, examines the distribution and abundance of human bodies and explores how these are influenced by interactions between individuals and their environment. The human body is a complex system, arising from the combination of individual atoms, molecules, polypeptides, and cells, which collectively give rise to emergent properties. The human body also serves as a medium for communication. Many individuals, either consciously or unconsciously, continuously send and receive non-verbal signals. This form of communication, known as body language, constitutes a significant component of paralanguage.
